title: Microownership handoff playbook (scratch)
content:
Context:
This is a personal scratchpad for a lightweight micro-ownership handoff pattern during PRs and small refactors. Goal is to reduce review friction and make post-merge follow-ups clear without huge docs. Keep things terse and action-oriented.

Principles (quick):
- Microownership: every change has 1 explicit owner for follow-ups (not just an author).
- Minimal friction: reviewers should be able to decide quickly (accept/reject/ask) with a tiny checklist.
- Signal-first comments: call out risk signals and required verification steps.
- Capture follow-ups inline so post-merge work is trackable.

Mini-rubric (score each 0-3 inline in PR description):
- Ownership clarity: 0=no owner; 1=author only; 2=author+oncall; 3=owner assigned + secondary
- Complexity: 0=tiny (1-3 LOC), 1=small (4-20), 2=moderate (21-150), 3=large/arch change
- Test coverage: 0=none, 1=manual steps, 2=unit tests, 3=automated e2e or infra tests
- Rollback cost: 0=can revert in <1 min, 1=requires DB migration undo, 2=stateful rollback steps, 3=manual coordinated rollback across teams

Sample PR header template to paste: (one-liner + rubric)
- Title: <short summary>
- Owner: <name/email>  // person who will do follow-ups
- Complexity: 1
- Tests: 2
- Rollback: 0
- Why: <why this change is needed, links to ticket/bug>
- Quick test: <how reviewer can validate in 2-3 steps>

Pre-review checklist (author):
- [ ] Smaller commit groups (rebase-squash per logical change)
- [ ] Add owner field in PR description
- [ ] Add minimal reproduction or smoke steps
- [ ] List any infra flags/config needed
- [ ] Note any user-facing surface or telemetry changes

Reviewer quick checklist: aim for a 5-minute decision loop.
- Safety signals (first): does this touch auth/telemetry/billing/storage? If yes, escalate to SRE/security.
- Correctness signals: skim algorithmic logic, edge cases, nil handling.
- Tests & assertions: do unit tests cover core paths? If not, leave a focused test request.
- Performance/regressions: any hotpath change? ask for a perf run or benchmark snippet.
- Accept criteria: leave final comment with one of Accept / Request changes / Needs discussion + 1-sentence reason.

Example reviewer comments (short templates):
- "Accept — small, owner={NAME}, smoke steps verified locally."
- "Request changes — see inline note about null handler at src/foo; please add unit + a short comment."
- "Needs discussion — this touches migration X, can we coordinate with migrations-oncall?"

Post-merge handoff notes (owner):
- Create a 1-line follow-up issue if further work needed (label: post-merge).
- Add a quick Slack note in #team with link + 1-line summary for oncall awareness if rollback cost >=1.
- Schedule a 15-min pairing session if complexity=3 and multiple modules affected.

Mini experiments to validate safety (run on new changes):
- Canary diff-sampling: select 3-5 recent PRs of similar size, run test coverage delta analysis to predict missing tests.
- Smoke-run script: simple script that runs a sequence of curl commands to critical endpoints (store as scripts/quick-smoke.sh in repo).
- Rollback rehearsal: for changes with rollback_cost>=1, rehearse a revert branch on a sandbox cluster and time it. Note duration.

Commands/cheatsheet (copy into PR if useful):
- quick local rebase/patch: git fetch origin && git checkout -b tmp && git cherry-pick <commit> && ./run-smoke.sh
- apply patch locally: git show <pr-commit> > /tmp/patch.diff && git apply /tmp/patch.diff && pytest -q tests/unit
- revert PR merge: git revert -m 1 <merge-commit> && push -f origin rollback/<pr-number> (coordinate w/owner)

Follow-up template (post-merge issue body):
- Summary: one sentence
- Owner: <name>
- Why now: link to PR + risk signals
- Steps: 1) add test 2) update docs 3) monitor metric X for 48h
- Acceptance: <what confirms done>

Unresolved questions (TODOs for me):
- How to embed the rubric scores into PR templates without adding noise for tiny PRs? toggle by label?
- Can we add a GH action that flags missing owner field and auto-assigns reviewer suggestions? (low friction)
- Should rollback rehearsals be required for rollback_cost>=2 or optionally suggested?

Quick notes / one-liners I keep forgetting:
- Always call out user-visible changes even for infra code.
- If you change telemetry keys, add both old and new in PR description so dashboards can be patched.
- Small refactors that touch critical code paths = invite at least one senior reviewer.

Open follow-ups (tracked locally):
- Add smoke script to repo (todo: put under tools/smoke/canary.sh) — assigned to Lina
- Prototype GH action to warn on empty owner field — spike next week (Omar)
